final_candidates.decision_summary: Y241 lies in the solvent-exposed GP1 231-250 region overlapping the mapped 12.1F/37.2D footprints; Tyr-to-His preserves aromatic character while altering hydrogen-bonding and contact chemistry. Conservative substitution reduces risk to folding and entry.

S246 sits in the same exposed GP1 epitope patch; Pro locally distorts backbone conformation and disrupts paratope contacts without ablating the fold. Moderate confidence due to unknown exact footprint boundaries.

F147 is in the GP1 141-150 loop implicated in neutralizing-antibody contact; replacing the large aromatic with Ser removes hydrophobic paratope contacts while likely preserving the loop core. Lower confidence because loop integrity effects are unverified.

stop_reason.detail: Self-iteration without external evidence is unlikely to improve the Top-3; final candidates selected from the round-1 pool.

history.rationale: Y241 sits in a solvent-exposed GP1 loop (residues ~230-260) that is a major neutralizing-antibody footprint; a conservative aromatic-to-aromatic substitution preserves local structure while altering antibody contact chemistry.
Y241 sits in the solvent-exposed GP1 231-250 region overlapping mapped footprints of 12.1F/37.2D; a Tyr->His charge/hydrogen-bond change is structurally conservative while perturbing contact.

Introducing a proline in the exposed GP1 loop between the 12.1F/37.2D contact region can reshape loop conformation to disrupt binding while minimally affecting the GP1 core needed for receptor binding and entry.
S246 lies within the same exposed GP1 epitope patch; Pro can locally alter backbone conformation and disrupt paratope contacts without ablating folding.

Charge reversal/substitution at Q247 in the same antigenic loop can break antibody H-bonding contacts; GPC internal folding and entry machinery are unlikely to be affected by this solvent-facing side chain.
Retained but slightly deprioritized; gain-of-charge mutations at epitope-proximal residues can reduce entry fitness in addition to antibody binding.
Removing a polar side chain at a predicted antibody-contact position in the GP1 loop reduces H-bonding potential with 12.1F-like antibodies with low structural disruption.
Conservative change with modest expected epitope disruption; kept as a lower-risk backup.
W264 lies near the GP1/GP2 interface region implicated in 8.9F binding; alanine here can weaken antibody contacts, though some risk to entry-associated conformational rearrangements.
W264 is near the GP1/GP2 cleavage-proximal region and may be structurally buried; Ala here risks destabilizing the prefusion trimer, so confidence is lowered.
A bulky hydrophobic substitution at this surface-adjacent position may sterically clash with antibody paratope contact residues while lying outside the receptor-binding site.
Sequence verification shows position 268 is D (Asp), not S — the candidate's WT residue is invalid and it must be removed.

rejection.reason: Sequence verification shows position 268 is D (Asp), not S — the candidate's WT residue is invalid and it must be removed.

history.rationale: H374 is in the GP2 heptad-repeat-adjacent region near 8.9F epitope space; mutation to arginine alters charge and antibody recognition but retains entry-critical coiled-coil packing probability.
H374 is within GP2 internal-facing elements likely not part of the neutralizing-antibody surface; deprioritized.
A conservative size reduction at a buried-adjacent epitope residue can subtly shift antibody-contact geometry with minimal folding risk.
Highly conservative substitution; predicted escape impact too small to justify a top slot, retained only for pool continuity.
F147 is in the 141-150 GP1 loop implicated in neutralizing-antibody contact; replacing a large aromatic with Ser removes hydrophobic paratope contacts while likely preserving the loop core.
N146D is a conservative-size but charge-introducing change in the same epitope loop, a common escape mechanism in arenavirus GP1.
